question: The Commission’s stance raises serious questions, as in response to a previous question1 by Kostas Papadakis highlighting the enormous shortages in personnel and infrastructure, it avoided making the slightest comment. However, it itself had initiated infringement proceedings for delays in the adoption of basic safety technologies at airports.

Air traffic control workers, pilots and other workers have repeatedly pointed out the problems of outdated communication infrastructure, non-functioning radar and serious shortages of personnel at all airports in the country. It is indicative that in August the radar on Mount Merenda in Attica was put out of operation. In view of the above: 1.

What is the Commission’s position on the fact that the shortage of air traffic control staff, the outdated infrastructure and the outdated control and warning system equipment, together with the intensification of and the deleterious standards of the EU guidelines for the flow of aircraft arrivals and departures – serving the profitability of airline groups and private airport owners – create a very dangerous backdrop for flight safety and ensuring the lives and safety of passengers and workers?

What prevented the Commission from responding to the substance of the issues raised by MEPs Kostas Papadakis and Lefteris Nikolaou-Alavanos in a previous question on flight safety issues, concealing the dangerous situation that exists, while it had sent a letter of notice to the Greek Government in April 2024 and a reasoned response last year in December on the basis of the Government assertions provided to it?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.3.2026) Civil aviation operates under common EU aviation safety rules. There can be no compromise on safety. The Hellenic Civil Aviation Authority (H-CAA) is responsible for ensuring compliance with EU legislation on Air Traffic Management (ATM) in Greece and for the oversight of the Hellenic Air Navigation Service Provider (HASP).

The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) supports the H-CAA by conducting standardisation visits and monitoring their safety oversight. The Commission expects that the recently adopted Greek Law No 5240/20251 will grant to HASP the necessary autonomy, resources and capabilities to invest in staff, including air traffic controllers, and technology.

The Commission finds this to be a crucial step to pave the way in addressing the current situation in Greece. There are three open infringement procedures regarding the deployment of datalink capabilities2, the deployment of radars3 and the publication of performance-based navigation procedures4.

The Commission services are in close contact with HASP and the Greek authorities and, with support from EASA, Eurocontrol and the SESAR Deployment Manager, review Greece’s regular progress reports on actions for prompt compliance with EU Law in the field of Air Traffic Management.

Following the incident resulting in the closure of the Greek airspace on 4 January 2026, the Greek Safety Investigation Authority is conducting an independent investigation that will propose recommendations to avoid similar incidents in the future. The H-CAA should determine if there is a need for HASP to take additional measures to ensure safety.
The Commission services and EASA will also analyse the results of the investigation for any further steps necessary at EU level.
1 Greek Law No 5240/2025 of 24 October 2025 on the establishment and organisation of the legal entity

governed by public law known as the Hellenic Aviation Service Provider and other provisions, published in the Government Gazette of the Hellenic Republic, Series I, No 184/24.10.2025. 2 https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/inf_24_4561, letter of formal notice sent on 03/10/2024. 3 https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/inf_25_2745, reasoned opinion adopted on 11.12.2025. 4 https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_25_2864, referral decision adopted on 11.12.2025.
